member.name: T:ComputeSharp.CompileOptionsAttribute
member.summary:
An attribute that indicates the compile options that should be used when compiling a given compute shader.
This attribute can be used to annotate shader types as follows:
[CompileOptions(CompileOptions.IeeeStrictness | CompileOptions.OptimizationLevel3)] struct MyShader : IComputeShader { }
This attribute can also be added to a whole assembly, and will be used by default if not overridden by a shader type.
member.param: The compiler options to use to compile the shader.

member.name: M:ComputeSharp.CompileOptionsAttribute.#ctor(ComputeSharp.CompileOptions)
member.summary:
An attribute that indicates the compile options that should be used when compiling a given compute shader.
This attribute can be used to annotate shader types as follows:
[CompileOptions(CompileOptions.IeeeStrictness | CompileOptions.OptimizationLevel3)] struct MyShader : IComputeShader { }
This attribute can also be added to a whole assembly, and will be used by default if not overridden by a shader type.
member.param: The compiler options to use to compile the shader.

member.name: P:ComputeSharp.CompileOptionsAttribute.Options
member.summary: Gets the compile options to use to compile the shader.

member.name: T:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions
member.summary: Flags to control the options that can be used to compile a compute shader.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.AllResourcesBound
member.summary: Enables agressive flattening.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -all-resources-bound.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.DisableValidation
member.summary: Directs the compiler not to validate the generated code against known capabilities and constraints. This option should only be used with shaders that have been successfully compiled in the past. DirectX always validates shaders before it sets them to a device.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -Vd.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.DisableOptimization
member.summary: Directs the compiler to skip optimization steps during code generation. This option should only be used for debug purposes.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -Od.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.AvoidFlowControl
member.summary: Directs the compiler to not use flow-control constructs where possible.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -Gfa.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.PreferFlowControl
member.summary: Directs the compiler to prefer using flow-control constructs where possible.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -Gfp.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.EnableStrictness
member.summary: Forces strict compile, which might not allow for legacy syntax. By default, the compiler disables strictness on deprecated syntax.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -Ges.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.IeeeStrictness
member.summary: Forces the IEEE strict compile which avoids optimizations that may break IEEE rules.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -Gis.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.EnableBackwardsCompatibility
member.summary: Enables backward compatibility mode.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -Gec.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.OptimizationLevel0
member.summary: Directs the compiler to use the lowest optimization level. If this option is set, the compiler might produce slower code but produces the code more quickly. This option should be set when shaders are developed iteratively, as it can reduce compilation times.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -O0.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.OptimizationLevel1
member.summary: Directs the compiler to use the second lowest optimization level.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -O1.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.OptimizationLevel2
member.summary: Directs the compiler to use the second highest optimization level.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -O2.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.OptimizationLevel3
member.summary: Directs the compiler to use the highest optimization level. If this option is set, the compiler produces the best possible code but might take significantly longer to do so. This option should be set for final builds of an application when performance is the most important factor.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -O3.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.WarningsAreErrors
member.summary: Directs the compiler to treat all warnings as errors when it compiles the shader code. This option is recommended for new shader code, so that warnings can be resolved and the number of hard-to-find code defects can be minimized.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -WX.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.ResourcesMayAlias
member.summary: Directs the compiler that UAVs (uniform access views) and SRVs (shader resource views) may alias.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -res-may-alias.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.StripReflectionData
member.summary: Strips the reflection data from the generated shader bytecode. The bytecode size will be significantly smaller, but trying to perform reflection on the shader will return inaccurate results. It is recommend if not reflection is used.
member.remarks: This flag maps to -Qstrip_reflect.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.CompileOptions.Default
member.summary: The default options for shaders compiled by ComputeSharp.
member.remarks: This option does not include a flag to pack matrices in column-major order on input and output from the shader, as that is always enabled by default (it is necessary to ensure the constant buffer matches the managed layout).

member.name: T:ComputeSharp.GeneratedComputeShaderDescriptorAttribute
member.summary:
An attribute that indicates that a given compute shader should have its associated descriptor code being generated.
This attribute can be used on shader types that are declared as :
[GeneratedComputeShaderDescriptor] partial struct MyShader : IComputeShader { }
The shader type must implement either or .
When a shader is annotated with , the source generator will also add to its implemented interfaces, and implement its APIs automatically.

member.name: T:ComputeSharp.GloballyCoherentAttribute
member.summary: An attribute that indicates that a field in a shader type should use the modifier.

remarks.para: The modifier causes memory barriers and syncs to flush data across the entire GPU such that other groups can see writes. Without this modifier, a memory barrier or sync will only flush a UAV within the current thread group.

In other words, if compute shader thread in a given thread group needs to perform loads of data that was written by atomics or stores in another thread group, the UAV slot where the data resides must be tagged as , so the implementation can ignore the local cache. Otherwise, this form of cross-thread group data sharing will produce undefined results.

member.name: T:ComputeSharp.RequiresDoublePrecisionSupportAttribute
member.summary: An attribute for a compute shader indicating that the shader requires support for double precision operations.
member.remarks: This attribute does not map to any HLSL feature or compile option directly, but it is needed to make using double precision operations opt-in. It is easy to accidentally introduce them in a shader when that is not intented, and doing so can make the shader run slower and not being compatible with some GPUs (eg. many arm64 GPUs lack support for double precision operations). To avoid this, support is disabled by default, and it is necessary to add this attribute over a shader type to explicitly allow using these operations.

member.name: T:ComputeSharp.ThreadIds.Normalized
member.summary: A that indicates the normalized ids of a given GPU thread running a compute shader. These ids represent equivalent info to those from , but normalized in the [0, 1] range. The range used for the normalization is the one given by the target dispatch size (see ).
member.remarks:
When the dispatch size on a given axis is 1, the normalized value along that axis will be 0. Otherwise, it will just be the normalization over [0, 1] for the current dispatch progress along that axis. That is, for instance:
[0].
[0, 1].
[0, 0.5, 1].
[0, 0.333..., 0.666..., 1].
[0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1].
And so on depending on the dispatch size along the requested dispatch axis.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.DeviceLostReason.DeviceHung
member.summary: The application's device failed due to badly formed commands sent by the application. This is an design-time issue that should be investigated and fixed.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.DeviceLostReason.DeviceRemoved
member.summary: The video card has been physically removed from the system, or a driver upgrade for the video card has occurred. The application should destroy and recreate the device.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.DeviceLostReason.DeviceReset
member.summary: The device failed due to a badly formed command. This is a run-time issue. The application should destroy and recreate the device.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.DeviceLostReason.DriverInternalError
member.summary: The driver encountered a problem and was put into the device removed state.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.DeviceLostReason.InvalidCall
member.summary: The application provided invalid parameter data. This must be debugged and fixed before the application is released.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.DeviceLostReason.AccessDenied
member.summary: The device was removed after attempting an invalid operation (eg. trying to write to the wrong swapchain buffer). The application should destroy and recreate the device. This also likely indicates an application bug.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.DeviceLostReason.UnspecifiedError
member.summary: The device was lost for an unspecified reason.

member.summary: Retrieves a wrapping instance for the input resource.
member.param: The input instance to create a wrapper for.
member.returns: An instance wrapping the current resource.

remarks.para: The returned instance can be used in a shader to enable texture sampling.

This is an advanced API that can only be used after the current instance has been transitioned to be in a readonly state. To do so, use , and specify . After that, this method can be used to get a readonly wrapper for the current texture to use in a shader. This instance should not be cached or reused, but just passed directly to a shader being dispatched through that same , as it will not work if the texture changes state later on. Before the end of that list of operations, the texture also needs to be transitioned back to writeable state, using the same API as before but specifying . Failing to do so results in undefined behavior.

member.exception: Thrown if the current instance or its associated device are disposed.
Thrown if the current instance is not in a readonly state.

member.name: M:ComputeSharp.Texture3DExtensions.ToArray``1(ComputeSharp.Resources.Texture3D{``0})
member.summary: Reads the contents of the current instance and returns an array.
member.typeparam: The type of items stored on the texture.
member.param: The input instance to read data from.
member.returns: A array with the contents of the current buffer.
member.remarks: The returned array will be using the same memory layout as the texture, that is, each 2D plane in the 3D volume represented by the texture is contiguous in memory, and planes are stacked in the depth dimension. This means that the resulting 3D array will have a size of [D, H, W].

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.GraphicsDevice.cachedPipelineData
member.summary: The list of cached objects for the current device.
member.remarks: A new entry is added to this list every time a shader is dispatched using this device. These cached items are stored via a , meaning they will be collected automatically when the device is collected. But, due to the fact that could happen at any time, a list is required to guarantee the additional references added by the native objects in the pipeline model can be released immediately.

member.name: E:ComputeSharp.GraphicsDevice.DeviceLost
member.summary: Raised whenever the device is lost.

remarks.para: "Device lost" refers to a situation where the GPU graphics device becomes unusable for further operations. This can occur due to GPU hardware malfunction, driver bugs, driver software updates, or switching the app from one GPU to another.
A lost device can no longer be used, and any attempt to do so will throw an exception. To recover from this situation, the app must create a new device and then recreate all its graphics resources.
This event will only be raised at most once for a given instance. Additionally, the event is raised asynchronously with respect to the device being lost, and on a thread pool thread.

Gets or creates the default instance for the current machine.
The default define is the first device supporting the required feature level that could be created when enumerating the available adapters in performance order. That is, it is conceptually equivalent to the first successfully created device from .
member.returns: The default instance for the current machine.
member.remarks:
The returned is cached across multiple invocations. In order to support device lost scenarios (see ) and due to how the DirectX 12 runtime handles caching of device instances, this method has the following behavior:
If no device has been created, create the default one, cache it, and return it.
If a cached device is available, return that.
If the returned device is disposed, the cache is reset.
If is called again after that, the returned device might map to a different adapter. This would be the case if the first device was lost due to the adapter being removed from the system.
There is one additional caveat to the list above: if is called, then that device is lost, then the returned instance is disposed incorrectly (eg. with some existing resources not being disposed, which would keep the underlying device object alive), calling again will result in an exception instead of a different device being returned. That is, if enumerating adapters and trying to create a device fails due to device lost (as opposed to other valid failures when trying to normally create a device), an exception will be thrown instead of just skipping that adapter, because that would mean a device had been created but incorrectly disposed.
member.exception: Thrown if the target device was lost and incorrectly disposed (see remarks).
Thrown if no adapter could be created (this should never be the case).

member.name: M:ComputeSharp.GraphicsDevice.EnumerateDevices
member.summary: Enumerates all the currently available devices supporting the minimum necessary feature level. Physical devices and integrated GPUs will be enumerated first, and the WARP device will always be last.
member.returns: A sequence of instances.

remarks.para: Creating a device is a relatively expensive operation, so consider using to be able to filter the existing adapters before creating a device from them, to reduce the system overhead.

This method might enumerate discrete graphics devices multiple times (with different values) when using RDP to connect to a different Windows machine. This is the expected behavior and matches what the underlying DirectX APIs report when enumerating graphics adaptors in this specific scenario.

member.name: M:ComputeSharp.GraphicsDevice.QueryDevices(System.Predicate{ComputeSharp.GraphicsDeviceInfo})
member.summary: Executes a query on the currently available devices matching a given predicate.
member.param: The predicate to use to select the devices to create.
member.returns: A sequence of instances matching .

remarks.para: Note that only devices matching the minimum necessary feature level will actually be instantiated and returned. This means that might not actually be used to match against all existing adapters on the current system, if any of them doesn't meet the minimum criteria, and that additional filtering might be done after the input predicate is invoked, so a match doesn't necessarily guarantee that that device will be returned.

Just like , this method might enumerate discrete graphics devices multiple times when using RDP to connect to a different Windows machine. This is the expected behavior and matches what the underlying DirectX APIs report when enumerating graphics adaptors in this specific scenario.

member.name: T:ComputeSharp.Interop.InteropServices
member.summary:
Provides methods to interoperate with the native APIs and the managed types in this library.
None of the APIs in perform input validation, and it is responsibility of consumers to ensure the input arguments are in a correct state to be used (eg. not disposed).
Manually interfering with the underlying COM objects for any of these types can result in issues if the operations are not done correctly, which can prevent other APIs from functioning as expected. Consumers should ensure the executed operations do not result in any errors. Furthermore, even when the reference count to the returned COM object is incremented, consumers should ensure that the owning objects will remain alive as long as the returned pointers are in use, to avoid unexpected issues. This is because the lifecycle of certain COM objects (eg. resources) is delegated to an internal allocator that relies on resources being disposed as soon as the relative allocation object is disposed.

member.summary: Creates a new instance with the specified paramters.

member.name: T:ComputeSharp.TextureView2D`1
member.summary: The type represents a view over a 2D texture allocated on host memory, providing APIs to easily manipulate its contents without having to manually deal with the internal alignment requirements of textures. As such, one key difference with and arrays is that the underlying buffer for a instance might not be contiguous in memory. All this logic is handled internally by the type and it is transparent to the user, but note that working over discontiguous buffers has a performance impact. It is recommended to execute as much computation on the GPU side as possible.
member.typeparam: The type of items in the current instance.

member.name: F:ComputeSharp.Shaders.Dispatching.D3D12GraphicsCommandListGraphicsResourceLoader.rootParameterOffset
member.summary: The offset into the compute root descriptor table for loaded resources.

remarks.para: This is used to correctly align the explicit resources captured by shaders, with the implicit ones that are injected by ComputeSharp. For instance, the constant buffer is always added automatically.

For compute shaders capturing an implicit texture, this is used to skip the first target resource, as that is loaded explicitly by the shader runner using the target texture passed in by the user, which is not actually captured by the shader itself. The target root descriptor table index is therefore 2 in this case, as it needs to skip not only the this implicit texture to draw on, but also the constant buffer with capture values.
